title: Big O Complexity
description: Learn how to analyze algorithm efficiency using Big O notation.
content:
# Big O Notation

Big O notation is used to describe the performance or complexity of an algorithm. It specifically describes the worst-case scenario.

## Common Complexities

- **O(1)** - Constant time
- **O(log n)** - Logarithmic time
- **O(n)** - Linear time
- **O(n log n)** - Linearithmic time
- **O(n²)** - Quadratic time
- **O(2ⁿ)** - Exponential time

title: Recursion Flow
description: Understand how the call stack works with recursive functions.
content:
# Recursion and the Call Stack

Recursion is when a function calls itself. Each call adds a new frame to the call stack.

## Key Concepts

- **Base Case** - The condition that stops recursion
- **Recursive Case** - Where the function calls itself
- **Call Stack** - Memory structure that tracks function calls
- **Stack Overflow** - When recursion goes too deep

title: Sliding Window Pattern
description: Learn the sliding window technique to optimize array and string problems.
content:
# Sliding Window Pattern

The Sliding Window pattern is used to perform a required operation on a specific window size of a given array or linked list, such as finding the longest subarray containing all 1s. Sliding Windows start from the 1st element and keep shifting right by one element and adjust the length of the window according to the problem that you are solving.

## When to Use It

- The problem involves a data structure that is ordered and iterable like an array or a string.
- You are asked to find a subrange in that array/string, like a longest, shortest or target value.
- There is an apparent naive or brute force solution that runs in O(N²), O(2^N) or some other large time complexity.

title: Graph Representations
description: Understand Adjacency Matrix vs Adjacency List for storing graphs.
content:
# Graph Representations

Graphs can be represented in memory in two main ways: Adjacency Matrices and Adjacency Lists. Choosing the right one is crucial for performance.

## Adjacency Matrix

A 2D array of size V x V where V is the number of vertices. If `adj[i][j]` is 1, there is an edge from i to j.
- **Space:** O(V²)
- **Pros:** Fast O(1) edge lookup.
- **Cons:** Wastes space for sparse graphs.

## Adjacency List

An array of lists. `adj[i]` contains a list of all neighbors of vertex i.
- **Space:** O(V + E)
- **Pros:** Saves space for sparse graphs. Fast to iterate over neighbors.
- **Cons:** Slower O(V) edge lookup.

title: Dynamic Programming Intro
content:
# Dynamic Programming

Dynamic Programming (DP) is a method for solving complex problems by breaking them down into simpler subproblems. It is applicable when subproblems overlap.

## Two Approaches

1. **Top-Down (Memoization):** Start solving the given problem by breaking it down. If you see that the problem has been solved already, then just return the saved answer. If it has not been solved, solve it and save the answer.
2. **Bottom-Up (Tabulation):** Analyze the problem and see the order in which the sub-problems are solved and start solving from the trivial subproblem, up towards the given problem.
